text: Stronger AI demand and more severe undersupply is driving higher pricing and margin assumptions for ABF substrates: We upgraded Unimicron and NYPCB on Feb 22, 2026 (report here). Recent checks indicate that ABF undersupply gap would widen to 22% by 2030 (vs 15% previously), which is putting upward pressure on pricing and margins for the substrate suppliers. Increasing constraints are also driving a broadening out of the supply ecosystem:

As demand gets stronger, we are seeing end-customers choosing to allocate more demand to smaller scale suppliers, as well as customers choosing to work with new entrants. This is why our recent checks indicate that Kinsus (not covered) is working on more different kinds of substrates for Nvidia, and ZDT is also working on qualification for future TPU substrates (in addition to being a key substrate supplier for China AI chips). We believe this is further evidence that customers are concerned about supply tightness and are finding different solutions to ensure business continuity. We upgrade ZDT to OW with new PT of NT\$570 (42% upside).

What are the risks? 1) Weaker demand for PCs, general servers, and AI servers; 2) meaningful capacity expansion plans; 3) T-glass being more constrained than we expect; 4) CoWoP displacing ABF substrates.

How Changes to Assumptions Change ABF S/D Dynamics

We now forecast ABF Supply/Demand imbalance to widen by 2030: After baking in latest assumptions and estimates, our bottom-up ABF substrate S/D model points to 22% undersupply by 2030 (vs \~15% previously). Why are our supply/demand dynamics largely similar in CY26-28, although demand has increased? This is because we bake in slightly stronger capacity expansion plans for Unimicron. At the beginning of this year, Unimicron only had plans to expand capacity by \~10% y/y, but that has changed in the past few months, and through more de-bottlenecking efforts, Unimicron is able to squeeze out \~40% additional capacity (if we compare YE26e to YE25) across all of its major production sites (four in Taiwan and one in China). Through utilizing all available space and increasing production efficiency, Unimicron is able to quickly add new capacity that can come online this year, compared to any greenfield capacity expansions that would typically take two or more years to bring online.

text: Where are we in the cycle?
The ABF substrate market has gone through a few cycles over the past two decades.
We are now still in the early innings of an up-cycle...

There was a prolonged down-cycle from 2012-18 as the PC TAM shrank amid the rise of smartphones and tablets. During this tough period, companies were not able to generate profit and had to compete on price to fill their idle capacity. As a result, during those years, there was no or very limited capacity expansion, and capital expenditure by the major ABF substrate suppliers was kept at a minimum (Exhibit 3).

Even as general server demand picked up, lifting utilization rates across the group going into 2020, ABF substrate suppliers remained cautious on the longer-term demand outlook and stayed disciplined, hesitant to expand capacity. Hence, capex turned up just slightly in 2019-2020, increasing \~US\$600mn vs. \~US\$2.2bn on average per year in 2012-18.

This underinvestment led to a sudden undersupply, as the shock from Covid-19 drove strong work-from-home demand for PCs, as well as increased data usage and storage for general computing driven by online entertainment. This ultimately led to a significant increase in ABF substrate market value between 2020-2022, driven by the sudden surge in demand, along with meaningful pricing adjustments owing to the lack of supply.

During this 2020-2022 period, a lot of capacity expansion was set in motion, as ABF substrate suppliers and customers came to agreement that necessary investments were needed for future growth. Some subsidies were even given to these suppliers to facilitate this capacity expansion. This is why capex jumped from \~US\$2.9bn in 2020 to US\$4.1bn in 2021 and US\$5.5bn in 2022; even in 2023-24 capex remained elevated, as capacity expansion plans continued.

Unfortunately, demand did not play out as expected. As the world came out of the pandemic, demand for PCs and online entertainment fell sharply. This normalization of demand, coupled with capacity expansion from practically every major ABF substrate supplier, resulted in the ABF substrate market once again becoming oversupplied. This led to a sharp decline in ABF substrate market value in 2023-24, as volumes normalized, driving prices down to normalize against the new supply/demand dynamic.

Fortunately, cloud demand remained strong for general computing, and with AI demand starting to pick up, the down-cycle this time around was much shorter (two years) vs. the prior down-cycle (six years).

In 1H24, the ABF substrate market troughed and we started to see an upward inflection since then, but the pace of the recovery has been moderate and bifurcated. Midrange/low-end markets such as PCs have shown moderate demand recovery, with high-end server and AI-related end-demand recovering and growing at a faster pace. This is why we turned the page on our bearish stance in 1H25, but did not turn more bullish until early 2026.

In 2015, we estimate that these segments combined were only \~10% of the market, but that rose to \~60% by 2025 and we expect it will account for 75%+ of the entire ABF substrate market value by 2030. In other words, server, AI GPU, AI ASIC, and networking-related applications have been the main growth driver for ABF substrate demand over the past decade and will remain a tailwind to drive even further growth in the coming years. text: What does this new S/D dynamic mean for pricing and margins?

We estimate cost inflation will drive ABF substrate pricing to grow 15-20% y/y in CY26, and 20%+ y/y in CY27 mainly driven by an imbalance in ABF substrate S/D. Because our view is that the imbalance will continue to widen in CY28 and thereafter, we are also assuming pricing will continue to move higher in CY28, in the range of 25-40% y/y, depending on the customer. For Unimicron, who has higher exposure to larger customers, we model another 20%+ pricing growth y/y for CY28, but for NYPCB, we estimate pricing growth will accelerate in CY28 to 40%+ y/y growth, given more severe ABF substrate supply shortage.

Any new capacity expansion plans will need at least two years to bring online: So any new meaningful capacity expansion plans that we hear from hereon out will only impact the S/D dynamics for CY29 onwards. So for the next two years, we just need to focus on the changes to end-demand when analyzing this space.
Supply constraints are causing an expansion of the ecosystem to enable more suppliers to move into the high-end

Since the beginning of the year, we have seen more developments happening in the supply chain. We feel like the ABF substrate ecosystem is broadening out to enable more suppliers to prove their capability. We believe this is due to constraints in supply. This is why we see companies like Kinsus (not covered) working on more Nvidia substrate solutions, and even expanding capacity to support more volumes from Nvidia.

Additionally, we also see ZDT's utilization rate climbing at its Shenzhen ABF factory, with the company mentioning that it has increased IC substrate revenue 60%+ y/y in 1Q26 and turned profitable for the first time in 1Q. ZDT also mentioned that it sees clear demand visibility for this business and targets to grow by 70%+ y/y for CY26, supported by the ramp-up of its Kaohsiung ABF fab this year for international customers. Moreover, ZDT is also advancing installation of its Shenzhen ABF Fab 2 to support future AI computing-related demand, which we believe is mainly supported by domestic China AI chip demand.

text: The 'agentic economy' is scaling faster than initially anticipated

Please see here for our Global Tech team's latest TAM forecast. In the report, our base-case total server CPU TAM rises 25% to US\$125B by 2030, driven by a US\$79B orchestration CPU layer on top of US\$45B host/cloud CPU TAM, which drives an incremental \~12-13M units of CPU by 2030. From US\$100bn CPU TAM to US\$125bn

In our initial note, Rise of the AI Agent - Global Implications, we parsed the Host CPUs from Orchestration CPUs. We used Mercury data to estimate the Host CPU market (Grace, Vera, Graviton etc) at US\$45bn by 2030. We continue to maintain this assumption in our new model. However, our previous estimates for the orchestration CPU TAM were conservative in particular our assumption for an AI semi TAM of US\$1.2trn, note Nvidia is talking to this being as large as US\$3-4trn. Our previous orchestration TAM of US\$30-60bn implied a CPU TAM of US\$105bn, in-line with Arm's commentary at Arm Everywhere (link). However, AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) is now talking to a level closer to US \$120bn.

In deriving the Orchestration CPU TAM we take two different approaches: (i) a bottom-up model identifying agents per session, concurrent usage of compute and instructions per token; and (ii) a top-down model identifying GW installed per annum, implied racks and the ratio of CPU:GPU.

text: Why are we upgrading ZDT to OW?
Server+Substrate Revenue will grow meaningfully over the next 2-3 years

IC substrate revenue to grow 3x by 2028: According to the company, IC substrate revenue grew 65% y/y in 1Q, which we believe is driven by increased demand and pricing for BT substrates, but also rising demand for ABF substrates. Zhen Ding is a key supplier of ABF substrates in China, utilizing its Shenzhen fab. In fact, the company mentioned that in 1Q26, its Shenzhen ABF fab has finally turned profitable, for the first time. We believe this means that utilization has risen to at least 60%+, and should only continue to grow from here. Our semiconductor team believes that China AI chips will see strong growth over the coming years, growing from \~0.5M units in 2024 to \~7M units by 2030. Our checks indicate that China AI chips use larger substrates, with higher layer count, compared to chips of similar performance from international chip vendors. This is most likely due to the sub-par chip design capabilities. But this becomes a positive for the substrate suppliers, as the pricing of the substrate is determined by the total size in demand. Other than seeing strong growth from China AI chips, we also see ZDT trying to qualify for Google TPU substrate, through MediaTek. If confirmed, this would be more meaningful to the sentiment of the stock than earnings, and help drive a re-rating. Because this would imply that ZDT has the capability to do high-end ASIC substrates, which would also allow ZDT to use that experience and project win to approach other ASIC or GPU customers.

However, in addition to ABF substrates, we also believe ZDT will continue to take share in BT substrates, as we see Unimicron ramping down its BT substrate capacity to focus more on ABF. We believe ZDT will take this opportunity to take more share in BT substrates. Additionally, more demand for memory would also mean more demand for BT substrates

AI-related PCB will also see strong growth in the coming years: ZDT has already been supplying a lot of general server and AI server peripheral PCBs. It acquired this capability when it acquired BoardTek in 2020. This will continue to grow and even accelerate in the coming years as other Tier1 AI server PCB suppliers are capacity constrained. This gives ZDT more room to expand this portion of its business. Additionally, our checks also indicate ZDT having passed qualification of Nvidia's compute HDI PCB for Rubin. While we believe ZDT's share will remain small, at 5% share, this would still contribute \~NT\$8B revenue annually, and ZDT is able to get its share up to 10%, it mean imply a \~NT\$16B annualized revenue contribution.

Other than this, ZDT is also a significant PCB supplier for optical transceiver modules. For 400G+, HDI PCB is required, and for 800G+ speeds, mSAP capability is needed. ZDT has had mSAP capability for a long-time, being one of the major substrate-like PCB (SLP) for Apple iPhone. This is one of the reasons why ZDT is a significant supplier for optical transceiver module PCBs. We estimate ZDT has \~25% supply share, which would mean that we expect NT\$14-15B revenue contribution this year, growing to \~NT\$25B in CY27. Because there is limited competition today, this business also carries high margin, which we estimate to be at least 40% GM, making it a sizeable profit contributor over the next 2-3 years.
